(is associated with: «German army sends combat engineers to help fortify Poland's border») -/Polnische Streitkräfte/dpa German army combat engineers are helping Poland fortify its border with Belarus and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, the Bundeswehr said on Wednesday, adding that the troops from a reinforced armoured engineer platoon had already arrived in early July. The soldiers are working alongside the Polish army to dig anti-tank ditches, erect tank barriers and build field fortifications and fighting positions. "The aim of this initiative is to delay an invasion by those forces in the event of a military conflict, thereby increasing the responsiveness of Polish troops and NATO," the Bundeswehr, as Germany's armed forces are formally known, said in a statement. Advertisement Advertisement Poland, an EU and NATO member and one of the strongest supporters of Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion, considers itself threatened by Moscow and is investing billions in what it calls the "Eastern Shield" - a fortified defensive line along parts of its eastern border. By the end of this year, the Polish Defence Ministry plans to secure around 250 kilometres of the eastern and northern border, with concrete fortifications, electronic surveillance systems and depots for engineer equipment. "The deployment of the Bundeswehr contingent is the first practical international assistance we have received for this project," Colonel Marek Pietrzak, spokesman for the Polish armed forces, told dpa. According to Polish figures, "several dozen" Bundeswehr engineers are stationed in the Masurian lake district at the Polish Land Forces training centre in Bemowo Piskie. The deployment is initially planned to run until the end of October. Advertisement Advertisement Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk commented on the Bundeswehr's deployment in his country on the platform X. "Polish and German soldiers are jointly reinforcing Poland's border with Russia. This sort of thing only happens under Tusk," he wrote, accompanied by a laughing emoji. This was a dig at his political opponents from the right-wing conservative PiS party. They are keen to stir up anti-German sentiment and regularly accuse Tusk of being controlled by Berlin. https://www.politico.eu/article/bernie-s.text: PARIS — Gabriel Zucman, an economist who became a household name in France last year thanks to his proposed wealth tax, is organizing a major summit on fiscal justice in Paris on Nov. 21 and has invited U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. “The explosion in extreme wealth and the accompanying concentration of power are disrupting our societies. It is this imbalance that the Paris summit aims to tackle,” Zucman said in an interview. “The aim is to provide an objective assessment of this new reality and to help forge the international partnerships that will ultimately enable democratic forces to prevail.” Zucman, who teaches at the Paris School of Economics and the University of California, Berkeley, is one of the world’s highest-profile advocates of taxing the ultra-wealthy. In recent months, he has campaigned for a California ballot initiative to levy a one-time state tax on billionaires equal to 5% of their net worth. Zucman and two fellow economists estimated the measure, Proposition 40, could bring in about $100 million in revenue. Advertisement Advertisement Zucman’s Paris event — currently billed as the “Summit Against the International Oligarchy” — is nominally focused on three themes: media and online platforms, artificial intelligence and taxing billionaires. But it won’t have an impact on the California contest, as voters there head to the polls on Nov. 3. Instead, it appears to be an opportunity to thrust wealth inequality and tax justice back into the public debate ahead of the next French presidential election, whose first round takes place in April of next year. The event, whose co-organizers include Nobel laureate Joseph Stiglitz and best-selling author Thomas Piketty, will kick off just a few days after the launch of Zucman’s similarly titled book, “Against the International Oligarchy.” Ocasio-Cortez, Sanders, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani — whom Zucman met in April — and top Mamdani aide Morris Katz were all invited, according to Pierre Natnaël Bussière, Zucman’s strategy and communications adviser. Representatives for Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire — who modeled parts of his campaign earlier this year on Mamdani’s — is slated to speak at a gala following the summit. While Grégoire has been trying to keep his focus local and beef up his image as a Paris-first leader, the unequal distribution of wealth and the growing proportion of wealth derived from inheritance are issues that affect housing prices and purchasing power in Paris — two key priorities for Grégoire. Anthony Lattier contributed to this report. Advertisement Advertisement

While authorities found no foreign involvement in the attacks – which left one school janitor dead and 11 injured across the Mazovia region – police inspected nearly 35,000 schools and detained 59 people as cyber defense units monitored digital threat channels. by TVP World | Oct. 10, 2026, 9:51 am Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of defence Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz delivers his speech during the official opening ceremony on the first day of the 34th International Defence Industry Exhibition in Kielce, Poland, 8 Sept. 2026. (Photo by Wojtek RADWANSKI / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Russia sought to exploit a series of violent school attacks in Poland to spread disinformation and sow panic, Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz has said, adding that Moscow sees a crisis and “immediately exploits it.” Poland, generally regarded as one of the EU’s safest countries, has been shaken by two knife attacks at schools in as many days, leaving one person dead and 11 others injured. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . The violence has prompted school closures and heightened security measures, while rumors of further attacks circulating online have fueled anxiety among parents. Speaking at a news conference on Friday, Kosiniak-Kamysz said he had received a report from Poland’s military cyber defense forces indicating that hostile actors were seeking to exploit the incidents. Advertisement “Yesterday evening also saw a major disinformation campaign that was certainly intended to spread panic,” he said. The minister did not establish a direct Russian involvement in the attacks themselves, but said exploiting crises was a longstanding feature of Moscow’s strategy. “They see a crisis situation and immediately exploit it,” he said. Kosiniak-Kamysz cited Russian disinformation during devastating floods that swept through southwestern Poland in September 2024, killing nine people and causing widespread destruction. At the time, false claims that hundreds of people had died circulated online. Violence shakes schools On Thursday, a 15-year-old former pupil attacked staff at a primary school in Leszczydół-Nowiny, a village northeast of Warsaw, killing a 37-year-old janitor and injuring two others. The teenager was wearing a helmet-mounted camera, which officials believe he intended to use to record or broadcast the attack. A day earlier, a 19-year-old attacked people with a machete-like knife at a school in Ostrołęka, also northeast of Warsaw, injuring nine people. Advertisement Police also detained a 17-year-old in the nearby town of Sierpc on Wednesday over an alleged plot to attack his school. All three incidents occurred in the Mazovia region, which includes the Polish capital. The violence prompted authorities in Wyszków municipality, which includes Leszczydół-Nowiny, to close primary schools and kindergartens on Friday, while other schools across the region canceled classes or switched to remote learning. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk on Thursday warned of a growing “cult of violence” and the risk of copycat attacks, calling for police to patrol every school in the country at least once a day. No evidence of online challenge Meanwhile, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said on Friday that investigators had found no evidence supporting rumors that the incidents were linked to an online challenge encouraging young people to commit acts of violence. “We want to make it very clear that we have analyzed all electronic devices seized during the operation, and as of today, there is no evidence confirming reports of a challenge among young people,” Kierwiński said. He added that authorities had found no concrete evidence linking the three incidents. Advertisement “I understand that emotions are running very high, but I urge everyone to rely exclusively on verified information,” he said, appealing to parents. Police had inspected 15,000 educational institutions nationwide and detained 19 people by noon Friday, with most cases involving what Kierwiński described as irresponsible behavior by young people. 59 detained nationwide Police said they had inspected nearly 35,000 educational institutions nationwide and detained 59 people by 5 p.m. Friday, as authorities stepped up security following the attacks. Around 24,000 police officers, supported by municipal guards, monitored schools and their surroundings throughout the day, while cybercrime officers and Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) monitored online activity. Police said officers had responded to 172 incidents involving reasonable suspicion of criminal activity and were continuing to monitor the internet around the clock.
